body:
Ohio's Housing Finance Agency conditionally awarded 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to Mercy on Main, a proposed 65-unit affordable apartment building at 907–917 E. Main St. in Columbus' Olde Towne East neighborhood — confirming the financing anchor the $22.8 million project needed to move forward.

## What the OHFA Award Unlocks

The 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit is the most competitive affordable housing financing tool administered by the Ohio Housing Finance Agency. Each year, OHFA reviews applications from developers statewide and makes conditional commitments to the strongest proposals; awardees can then sell the credits to investors to cover a majority of development costs, using the proceeds to reduce the amount of debt required.

Mercy on Main was one of 25 Ohio developments to receive conditional commitments in [OHFA's May 2026 round](https://ohiohome.org/news/releases/2026/9percent-taxcredits.aspx), which distributed more than $39.1 million in annual federal 9% tax credits selected from 62 statewide applications requesting more than $98.4 million. The full financing package for Mercy on Main, as reported in the OHFA announcement, also includes a $4 million permanent mortgage and $3.25 million in City of Columbus HOME funds, bringing total confirmed financing to approximately $22 million against the $22.8 million project cost. CREN was unable to directly retrieve the OHFA press release to confirm the per-project credit allocation; the specific figures cited here are drawn from the search-indexed OHFA announcement and the developer's own press release at [kingsleyandcompany.com](https://www.kingsleyandcompany.com/post/kingsley-co-expands-affordable-housing-efforts-into-columbus-with-mercy-on-main).

## A Zone In Success Story

Mercy on Main's five-story design would not have moved forward under Columbus's pre-2024 zoning code, which required a variance for buildings that height on E. Main St. Phase One of the city's Zone In reform — passed by City Council in July 2024 and applied to main street corridors including East Main — established by-right height allowances permitting five-story structures without a case-by-case hearing.

[Kingsley + Co.'s press release](https://www.kingsleyandcompany.com/post/kingsley-co-expands-affordable-housing-efforts-into-columbus-with-mercy-on-main) cited the Zone In corridor designation as a reason the East Main site was viable for their first Columbus project. That zoning connection extends beyond this one building: Zone In Phase Two — covering an additional 41 percent of the city and currently open for public comment through October 24, 2026, at columbus.gov/zoningupdate — is the direct successor to the reform that enabled Mercy on Main, and the project is an early test case of what Phase One's by-right changes have already made possible on a previously constrained corridor.

## Who Is Behind the Project

Kingsley + Co. is a Cincinnati-based affordable housing developer founded by Chinedum Ndukwe, a University of Notre Dame graduate and former NFL defensive tackle who played for the Cincinnati Bengals and Oakland Raiders before retiring from professional football in 2012. He is originally from central Ohio and formed the company shortly after leaving the game. The OHFA award represents Kingsley + Co.'s first 9% LIHTC development in Columbus; the firm has previously completed LIHTC-financed projects in Cincinnati.

The project is named for Mercy Okoronkwo, Ndukwe's grandmother. [NBC4 WCMH-TV reported](https://www.nbc4i.com/news/local-news/columbus/retired-nfl-player-behind-affordable-housing-proposal-in-columbus-olde-towne-east/) on the Columbus proposal when it was first announced, noting Ndukwe's central Ohio roots as a stated reason for expanding into the market.

## What the Neighborhood Gets

The proposed building would add 8 studio, 29 one-bedroom, 18 two-bedroom, and 10 three-bedroom units to E. Main St., targeted at households earning between 50 and 80 percent of the Area Median Income. Projected rents range from approximately $867 to $1,522 per month, per figures cited in the developer's announcement.

The 907–917 E. Main St. site sits on the East Main corridor, which COTA has designated as a planned Bus Rapid Transit route, and is within walking distance of the Near East Transit Center. That transit access is directly relevant to the income range the project targets, where car-free or car-light households are more common. [Columbus Underground described the site as underused](https://columbusunderground.com/affordable-housing-development-proposed-for-near-east-side-bw1/) when the proposal was first announced.

Olde Towne East's for-sale market has climbed considerably above the city average: Redfin data placed the neighborhood's median sale price at approximately $482,000 as of mid-2026, compared with the $350,000 Columbus metro median reported by Columbus REALTORS for July 2026. That gap between ownership and rental costs makes affordable rental supply on the East Main corridor a distinct housing need from the broader market — a gap Mercy on Main is designed to address.

## What Remains Uncertain

An OHFA conditional commitment is not a construction guarantee. Projects must still satisfy OHFA's compliance requirements, close all financing pieces, and clear any remaining municipal approvals before work can begin. The City of Columbus HOME allocation cited in the OHFA announcement has not been independently confirmed by CREN from city budget or grant records. Kingsley + Co. has not publicly announced a construction start date or a Development Commission hearing date for Mercy on Main as of August 27, 2026.

The next verifiable checkpoint: a Development Commission agenda listing for the 907–917 E. Main St. site at the Columbus Planning Division, a Kingsley + Co. announcement of a groundbreaking date, or OHFA documentation that the project has closed its financing.

---

*Sources: [OHFA May 2026 9% tax credit award announcement](https://ohiohome.org/news/releases/2026/9percent-taxcredits.aspx) · [Kingsley + Co. press release on Mercy on Main](https://www.kingsleyandcompany.com/post/kingsley-co-expands-affordable-housing-efforts-into-columbus-with-mercy-on-main) · [NBC4 WCMH-TV](https://www.nbc4i.com/news/local-news/columbus/retired-nfl-player-behind-affordable-housing-proposal-in-columbus-olde-towne-east/) · [Columbus Underground](https://columbusunderground.com/affordable-housing-development-proposed-for-near-east-side-bw1/) · [NH&RA / Housing Online (OHFA award trade coverage)](https://www.housingonline.com/2026/05/26/ohio-housing-finance-agency-awards-more-than-39-1-million-in-annual-9-tax-credits-for-affordable-housing-in-ohio/)*
